correctness.rationale: The ordered degree profile and reachability classification leave seven five-arc candidates, five strongly connected. Their exact polynomials are computed independently by Newton traces and the Leibniz determinant and give the three claimed Perron roots. Exact inequalities alpha<2^(1/3)<sqrt(phi), and alpha<5/4<2^(1/3), complete the thresholds. Exhaustive exact classification of all strongly connected digraphs on at most three vertices proves the minimal vertex order; four arcs on four vertices force a directed cycle. The local extinction Jacobian supplies the stated strict-stability regime only.

originality.rationale: Within inspected evidence, the fixed-bidegree exact five-route spectral classification and the zero-reciprocity stability split are not implied by the published large-network approximation, degree bounds, or undirected extremal theorems. The claim is a smallest-size finite classification, not a claim that graph topology can never affect persistence. Historical priority remains provisional because complete full-text access to some older papers was unavailable.

value.rationale: This is a complete small-structure boundary for a motivated ecological question: whether local in/out degree data and reciprocity suffice to predict invasion stability. The smallest relevant patch and route budgets, five labeled realizations in three spectral classes, and an explicit rational demographic parameter with opposite qualitative stability in two zero-reciprocity networks provide a reusable benchmark. The finding does not rely solely on novel code or a tiny numerical improvement.
